title: revamp-release-signing-and-introduce-lightweight-build-cache
author: Daniel Cho
description: Motivation: our release pipeline currently re-builds large artifacts for every minor change and signs assets with a fragile user-key flow. This PR introduces a compact, content-addressable build cache for CI and a deterministic release-asset signing step that uses a short-lived signing key stored in the infra vault. Goals: (1) reduce CI wall time and egress by avoiding full artifact rebuilds when inputs are unchanged; (2) make release signing auditable and retry-safe; (3) move heavy packaging into a nightly job while keeping fast deploys for hotfixes. What this PR does: - adds a lightweight build cache that keys on a deterministic hash of inputs (package.json, go.mod, Dockerfile, and the build script). Cache is stored in S3-compatible object storage with TTL and soft-eviction policy. - introduces a new GitHub Action (actions/release-sign) pinned to a SHA that obtains a scoped ephemeral signing key from Vault, signs release artifacts with RFC 8693-compatible metadata, and uploads detached signatures (.sig) alongside assets. - splits the existing release workflow into two workflows: release-fast (used for merging minor fixes; reuses cache and attaches unsigned artifacts if signing fails with a soft-fail policy) and release-full-nightly (rebuilds everything, signs with long-lived infra key, and populates the stable release channel). - pins a handful of popular actions to SHAs (checkout, setup-node, cache) and replaces the monolithic docker build step with a multi-stage, cached build that reduces image layers. - removes legacy script bin/ci-prepare-lockfile which previously converted between yarn and npm lockfiles; we now standardize on package-lock.json. - updates docs and release notes generator to include signature verification instructions and revocation list pointers. Backwards compatibility: older releases remain verifiable. Rollout plan: enable for all merges to main as a feature flag, monitor cache hit-rate and signing latency, then flip soft-fail to hard-fail after 2 weeks if metrics are stable. Checklist: - [x] design doc in Linear ENG-8342 - [x] smoke test: local cache hits on repeated builds - [x] e2e: release-fast created unsigned asset after simulated signing transient failure - [x] security review completed (keys lifecycle) - [x] docs updated (release/README.md) Related: Linear ENG-8342, ENG-9001. Notes: this does not attempt to change Dedicated deployment packaging. For more details see the inline CI workflow snippets and the commit messages below.

release_notes: - Introduce content-addressable lightweight build cache to reduce CI build time and egress. - Add deterministic release signing using ephemeral keys and upload detached signatures. - Split release pipelines into release-fast (fast merges, soft-signing failover) and release-full-nightly (full rebuilds + infra signing). - Pin key GitHub Actions to SHAs and refactor Dockerfile for cached multi-stage builds. - Remove legacy lockfile conversion script.
